To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age specific prevalence of RP in Denmark increases steeply from 1 in 100,000 at birth to 1 in 1,000 at age 5.
the prevalence of retinal dystrophies is higher than previously thought, and that the age specific prevalences are higher than expected.
The age specific prevalences for tapeto-retinal diseases in the Danish child populations are high, especially in the early childhood.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) The prevalence of tapeto-retinopathies in Denmark, (2) The genetic background of tapeto-retinales in Denmark, (3) The genetic background and clinical characteristics of cone-rod dystrophy in Denmark, (4) The genetic background, clinical features and prognosis of Leber congenital amaurosis in Denmark.
the epidemiology of retinal dystrophies in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of non-systemic tapeto-retinal degenerations is higher than previously thought and that the prevalence of X-linked tapeto- retinal dystrophies is lower than expected.
the prevalence of tapeto-retino- dystrophies among children is high.
the prevalence rate of RP in Danish children is 1 in 10,000 and that the most frequent genetic type is autosomal recessive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a significant proportion of early infantile, non-systemic tapeto-retinal degenerations are cone-rod dystrophy types.
the prevalence rates of RP in childhood have been overestimated.
the prevalence of tapeto-retinopathies among Danish children is high, and that there is an urgent need for a better knowledge of the genetic background and the pathogenetic mechanisms of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age at which a diagnosis is made is a major determinant of the clinical phenotype and the mode of inheritance.
the prevalence rate of tapeto-retinopathies is higher than previously estimated and that the prevalence of the different types of tapeto-retino-pathy varies considerably with age.
a large number of cases of tapeto-retina dystrophies are still not recognized or reported.
